title: Experimental and NOx abatement analysis of a VCR engine running on grape seed biodiesel diesel mixtures with MgO nanoparticles using an AI‐based approach
content:
Abstract

This study investigates B25 fuel, comprising 25% grape-seed biodiesel and 75% diesel, with 75 ppm magnesium oxide (MgO) nanoparticles in a variable compression ratio (VCR) diesel engine. Combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of diesel (B0), B25, and B25 + MgO were evaluated at injection pressures of 700, 750, and 800 bar. MgO improved fuel atomization, ignition quality, and oxidation behavior, influencing combustion phasing and heat-release characteristics. Compared with B25, B25 + MgO achieved a 23% increase in brake thermal efficiency (BTE) and a 19% reduction in brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC). Effects on carbon monoxide (CO), unburned hydrocarbons (HC), nitrogen oxides (NO x ), and smoke opacity varied with injection pressure. The CO and smoke reduction percentages require confirmation using original experimental measurements. ANOVA indicated statistically significant effects of MgO addition and injection pressure on BTE, BSFC, and emissions at the 95% confidence level. The NO x reduction may be associated with changes in ignition delay, premixed heat-release intensity, combustion phasing, and potential catalytic or oxygen-buffering effects of MgO, rather than reduced bulk in-cylinder temperature alone. Best overall performance occurred at 750 bar. An artificial neural network (ANN) model explored NO x prediction using engine load, injection pressure, and MgO concentration as inputs. Its accuracy was limited, indicating the need for improved data, additional inputs, and independent external validation. Overall, MgO-enhanced grape-seed biodiesel shows potential for improving diesel engine performance and influencing emissions, although further validation is needed to confirm emission reductions and predictive reliability.
